instruments.name: Player Stratocaster
instruments.tagline: The working Strat. Learn every part.
instruments.story: A useful place to learn a floating bridge and a three-pickup circuit without confusing “made in Mexico” with one universal specification. This reference is the original Player SSS. Confirm the actual instrument before borrowing a drawing or buying a part.
instruments.photo_credit: Chicago Music Exchange • representative 2021 Player, not your instrument
identity_checks: Check rear headstock model/origin and serial; record them without posting a full serial publicly.
Count three single-coil pickups and two bridge pivots. HSS and older Standard models need different references.
Photograph existing wiring before any work; a used guitar may no longer have its factory harness.

nodes.title: Strings & tuning
nodes.what: Separate string slip, nut binding and bridge movement before blaming the tuners.
checks: Tune to your usual tuning and note which strings move.
Check neat wraps and a seated string end without removing hardware.
Bend, retune and record the result; compare ordinary playing with tremolo use.
nodes.stop: A damaged nut, cracked headstock or a stuck adjustment needs a technician; do not file slots as a first diagnostic step.
nodes.tools: Tuner • spare matching strings • soft cloth

nodes.title: Neck & frets
nodes.what: Relief, saddle height and fret condition answer different questions. A truss rod is not a universal buzz control.
checks: Map the affected strings and frets at normal playing force.
Measure and record relief before changing anything.
Compare the measured setup with the applicable Fender guide; inspect for isolated fret problems.
nodes.stop: Stop at resistance, a damaged nut or uncertain tool fit. Do not prescribe a quarter-turn without a measurement.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Tremolo & saddles
nodes.what: This two-pivot bridge balances string pull against rear springs. A gauge or tuning change can move that balance.
checks: Photograph the resting bridge angle.
Confirm gauge/tuning matches your previous setup.
Record whether it is intentionally floating or decked before asking for an adjustment.
nodes.stop: Do not turn loaded pivot posts, add random springs or copy six-screw instructions onto this two-point bridge.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Pickups & controls
nodes.what: Five selector positions route three passive single coils. The workshop map explains selection; the factory drawing shows the connections.
checks: Use a known-good cable into a clean, low-volume amp.
Compare all five positions with volume and tones up.
Note whether noise changes when you move away from power supplies; document the actual pickup/harness before rewiring.
nodes.stop: Unplug for wiring work. Never bypass amplifier safety grounding or treat a shock as normal pickup noise.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Output jack & cable
nodes.what: A bad cable and an intermittent jack can look identical until isolated.
checks: Swap only the cable, then repeat the same movement gently.
Try the guitar directly, bypassing pedals.
Record whether the plug or the plate appears loose.
nodes.stop: Do not spin the jack nut freely: the internal wires may twist. A tech can hold the jack body and inspect the solder joints.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Parts fit & care
nodes.what: Model-family identification is the first step in any upgrade. Similar-looking pickguards and bridge parts need not match.
checks: Write the 014450 family and installed modifications in the passport.
Compare mounting holes, string spacing and pot/knob fit before ordering.
Keep removed parts and photograph the original arrangement.
nodes.stop: No drilling, routing or forced screw fit to make an unverified part work.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

instruments.name: American Professional II Stratocaster
instruments.story: The American profile gets its own electrical map, not a more expensive version of the Mexican page. The SSS American Professional II adds the neck pickup with a push-push tone control. A modified example or an HSS version may behave differently.
instruments.photo_credit: Fender • representative American Professional II SSS
identity_checks: Verify American Professional II, not American Professional I, Ultra or American Vintage.
Confirm SSS pickups and a push-push second tone control. The HSS version uses a different switching feature.
Record serial, installed pickups and any replacement harness before using the Downloads drawing.

nodes.title: Strings & tuning
nodes.what: Establish whether the problem follows a new string set, a tuning change or tremolo use.
symptoms: Tuning drifts after a string change
checks: Record string gauge and tuning.
Tune, play a short repeatable phrase and record which strings move.
Compare the result with the tremolo untouched, then with gentle use.
nodes.stop: Do not swap tuners or force the arm to diagnose a nut or balance problem.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Deep-C neck & setup
nodes.what: Comfort and measurements are separate: the named neck shape does not determine the correct relief or action for your playing.
checks: Record the troublesome frets and your tuning.
Measure relief and action separately, using the measurement locations in Fender’s guide.
Bring the measurements and a recording to a tech before requesting fretwork.
nodes.stop: A persistent isolated high fret or an unresponsive truss rod is not solved by repeated tightening.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Two-point tremolo
nodes.what: Keep the reference bridge hardware and the current owner’s settings distinct.
checks: Check the resting angle and spring arrangement visually.
Confirm the exact bridge/arm version in the factory service download.
Record floating/decked preference before changing gauge or setup.
nodes.stop: Do not apply older threaded-arm instructions to an unfamiliar arm socket, or adjust loaded pivots blindly.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: V-Mod II & neck-add switch
nodes.what: The SSS push-push control adds the neck pickup in positions 1 and 2; it is not a humbucker coil split.
checks: With clean low-volume amplification, compare position 1 with the push-push off and on.
Repeat in position 2; use the interactive map below to follow the selected pickups.
If operation differs, document your harness and compare the SSS factory service drawing, not a generic Strat diagram.
nodes.stop: Switch failure, a replaced pot or soldering work requires the exact drawing and competent bench work.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Signal chain & output
nodes.what: First isolate guitar, cable, pedals and amplifier so a symptom has a location.
checks: Use a known-good cable direct to the amp.
Compare normal and neck-add selections without changing the amp settings.
Record whether moving the plug alone recreates the fault.
nodes.stop: Never open amplifier electronics. Stop using equipment that produces shocks or burning smells.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Compatibility & preservation
nodes.what: American manufacture is not a guarantee that every US Strat component fits.
checks: Match the service model number and compare screw pattern.
Keep the push-push feature in the requirements for a replacement harness.
Save the original parts and annotate any changed function in the journey.
nodes.stop: Do not remove a function accidentally or route the body to compensate for a wrong part.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

instruments.name: 1959 Les Paul Standard
instruments.identity: Original-vintage reference • not a modern reissue
instruments.story: An original 1959 instrument calls for a conservation-first workbench. This is not a claim that you own an authenticated Burst. Originality, repairs and individual measurements remain unknown until inspected. The linked #9 0435 is one documented example, not a template for every surviving guitar.
instruments.photo_credit: The Music Emporium • inspected 1959 example #9 0435; not your instrument
identity_checks: Record provenance and repair documents; serial alone does not authenticate a vintage guitar.
Have a vintage specialist distinguish original 1959, Historic reissue and modified instruments.
Do not assume PAF readings, pot values, harness layout or bridge orientation from one pictured example.

nodes.title: Strings & headstock
nodes.what: Observation and a repeatable tuning test come before touching delicate or historic hardware.
checks: Record the current string set and tuning.
Photograph the headstock and tuner hardware without removing anything.
Give the tech a short recording of the tuning behavior and note any known repairs.
nodes.stop: Visible cracks, moving tuner hardware or an uncertain repair history mean stop and seek an in-person assessment.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Frets & structural condition
nodes.what: Fret wear, past refrets and neck repairs are part of an individual instrument’s history.
checks: Map the exact string and fret that misbehaves.
Record action and relief without adjusting them.
Compare with documented prior setup and repair records, not a modern reissue’s specification sheet.
nodes.stop: No fret filing, nut cutting, neck removal or blind truss-rod turns on an unassessed vintage guitar.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: ABR-1 & stopbar
nodes.what: Bridge orientation, saddle wear and past replacement parts must be documented before a setup change.
checks: Record an open note and the gently fretted 12th-fret note after tuning.
Photograph saddle orientation and stopbar height.
Ask a vintage specialist to inspect possible wear or replacement hardware.
nodes.stop: Do not flip saddles, file slots, bend posts or force a seized screw as a first response.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: PAFs & 1950s topology
nodes.what: The learning map shows two pickup branches and the selector. A 50s-style tone branch attaches at the volume output; that is a circuit concept, not proof of authenticity.
checks: At low volume, compare neck, both and bridge with both volume knobs up.
Record each control’s behavior without opening the pickup or disturbing solder.
Use ThroBak’s two-conductor drawing only as a specialist reference for an inspected harness.
nodes.stop: Do not desolder original joints, remove covers or pot pickups to test a theory. A vintage-qualified repairer should assess first.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Jack plate & selector
nodes.what: Fragile plastic and aged joints deserve support rather than force.
checks: Substitute a known-good cable with the amp low.
Observe whether the jack plate moves or has cracks.
Document the position and symptom; preserve any original parts removed by a professional.
nodes.stop: Do not tighten against cracked plastic or twist the jack and its wires.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Finish & provenance
nodes.what: The journey is an evidence log: dates, condition, repairs, removed parts and who did the work.
checks: Photograph condition under ordinary light before cleaning.
Use a clean soft dry cloth for a conservative surface wipe; obtain finish-specific advice for anything more.
Keep appraisal/provenance documents privately; share redacted details in forums.
nodes.stop: No solvent experiments, refinishing, drilling or “upgrades” before discussing preservation with a vintage specialist.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

instruments.name: Multiac Nylon Encore
instruments.tagline: Nylon feel. A stage-ready signal path.
instruments.story: The nylon workbench is deliberately different: string anchoring, a saddle transducer, body sensing, blend and powered electronics. It must not inherit Strat pickup-height instructions or a magnetic-pickup solder diagram. Confirm the electronics revision on your actual Encore.
instruments.photo_credit: Godin Guitars • representative Multiac Nylon Encore Natural SG
identity_checks: Read the model label and distinguish Encore from SA, ACS and Grand Concert.
Identify the preamp revision with Godin using serial and control-panel photos.
Confirm the specified nylon string set/tension and the correct battery information before replacing either.

nodes.title: Nylon strings & tie block
nodes.what: New nylon strings and a slipping tie end require a different diagnosis from steel-string electric hardware.
checks: Record the nylon set and tension category.
Inspect tie ends and roller windings visually, keeping the cedar top protected.
Use the maker’s restringing guidance or have a technician demonstrate the anchoring method before your first change.
nodes.stop: Never install a steel electric/acoustic set. Stop at a lifting bridge, damaged tie block or top crack.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Neck & nylon action
nodes.what: Do not apply an electric Strat action target to a nylon instrument without considering its construction and playing style.
checks: Record tuning, string type and where buzzing occurs.
Measure before changing anything and note recent temperature/humidity changes.
Ask Godin or a nylon-experienced tech for the correct setup baseline for the exact model.
nodes.stop: Do not sand the saddle or turn a truss rod based on a measurement meant for another instrument.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Saddle & transducer contact
nodes.what: The undersaddle source makes saddle seating part of the signal system as well as the string support.
checks: Compare each string unplugged, then amplified at the same setting.
Record which source/blend setting exposes the imbalance.
Check whether the symptom began after a string or saddle change.
nodes.stop: Do not shim, sand or lift the saddle or disturb transducer leads to experiment; request the correct service procedure.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Blend, EQ & preamp
nodes.what: This reference blends an undersaddle source with body sensing. It is not two magnetic pickups or a 13-pin synth map.
checks: Start at low system volume with EQ near its neutral positions.
Compare the two ends of the blend control and record the result.
Check the specified power source, then compare direct amplification before adding pedals or processing.
nodes.stop: No passive-Strat rewiring, phantom-power assumptions or battery substitutions without the correct revision documentation.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Power & output
nodes.what: A weak power source and an intermittent cable can both cause amplified problems.
checks: Test with a known-good cable and receiving input.
Check the battery type/polarity specified on your actual instrument or its manual.
Record whether a correct fresh battery resolves the symptom; ask Godin for the correct schematic if it does not.
nodes.stop: Do not short contacts, probe a live preamp casually or substitute an unverified power adapter.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Cedar top & stage care
nodes.what: Protect the instrument mechanically while tracing feedback and handling issues.
checks: Reduce level and change position relative to the speaker before altering the guitar.
Record the blend/EQ settings and sound-system arrangement.
Store safely away from sudden heat or moisture changes; log changes rather than guessing a cause.
nodes.stop: Top cracks, lifting seams or moving bridge hardware need a qualified repairer.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

instruments.name: Sonic Stratocaster HT H
instruments.story: A low-cost guitar deserves the same care, not a thinner page. The hardtail and single humbucker make this a clear starting point for learning a signal path and keeping useful setup records. Measure a proposed upgrade before spending more than the problem warrants.
instruments.photo_credit: Fender / Squier • Sonic Stratocaster HT H in Black
identity_checks: Verify HT H on the product/model reference, not the three-single-coil Sonic Strat.
There should be one bridge humbucker, a fixed bridge and two knobs; no selector is expected.
Document any replaced pickup and actual pot/switch hardware before using a generic wiring diagram.

nodes.title: First string change
nodes.what: A dependable baseline helps separate old strings from setup and hardware problems.
checks: Write down the installed gauge or mark it unknown.
Use a compatible steel electric set and record the change.
Tune, play and retune, checking that string ends and wraps are seated.
nodes.stop: Do not overtighten tuner screws or switch to a radically different gauge without planning a setup check.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Playability before upgrades
nodes.what: A useful setup diagnosis starts with the actual frets and strings, not the price on the headstock.
checks: Note affected strings/frets and photograph visible problems.
Record relief and action without assuming the factory shipping setup is still present.
Ask for a setup/fret assessment before buying pickups to fix a mechanical issue.
nodes.stop: Sharp fret ends, nut filing and fret leveling are technician tasks for a first-time owner.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Hardtail & intonation
nodes.what: A fixed bridge removes tremolo-spring balancing from this model’s checklist.
symptoms: Chords sound out of tune up-neck
checks: Tune the open string, then compare a gently fretted 12th-fret note.
Write sharp/flat per string before considering saddle movement.
Check correct tool fit against the exact factory specification; change only a measured adjustment and retune.
nodes.stop: Do not strip a small saddle screw, force a seized part or search for a nonexistent tremolo cavity.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: One humbucker, two controls
nodes.what: There is no pickup-selector fault to diagnose on a stock HT H. Trace pickup to volume/tone to jack.
checks: Use a clean amp, known-good cable and both controls up.
Compare volume and tone separately while playing the same phrase.
Record modifications; a generic one-humbucker drawing is a reference, not verified factory lug placement.
nodes.stop: Disconnect before internal work. Do not invent a coil-split option just because the pickup is a humbucker.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Cable, jack & loose hardware
nodes.what: The least expensive external check comes before a replacement pickup.
checks: Try a known-good cable direct to the amplifier.
Gently compare plug movement with ordinary playing.
Inspect whether the jack plate or nut moves; log the result.
nodes.stop: Do not turn the complete jack inside the body or bypass electrical safety grounding.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

nodes.title: Upgrade budget & fit
nodes.what: Keep a parts plan tied to an observed problem, with cost and fit written down first.
checks: Record the issue, the proposed part and the expected benefit.
Measure string spacing, mounting pattern and cavity clearance before ordering.
Compare the total installed cost with a professional setup and keep the original parts.
nodes.stop: No forced screws, drilling or routing based on the assumption that every Strat-shaped part is interchangeable.
nodes.tools: Tuner • good light • a written baseline

disclaimer: Reference profiles, not verified inspections of your instruments. Local notes stay in this browser; exports are your backup. No account sync, live source monitoring or automated repair diagnosis.
bench_note: Start unplugged for inspection. For amplified checks, use safe equipment at low volume. Never open an amplifier or defeat its safety grounding. Stop at cracks, a lifting bridge, electrical shocks, uncertain wiring or resistance to adjustment.

steps.title: Identify
steps.text: Confirm model, modifications and the exact document before touching a screw.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Reproduce one symptom at a time with a known-good signal chain.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Write a baseline, tuning and string set. Separate a measurement from a target.

steps.title: Act conservatively
steps.text: Make only an appropriate, understood adjustment; ask a technician when the evidence is unclear.

steps.title: Check & record
steps.text: Repeat the same test, compare the result and save what actually happened.
